subject: Franska
title: Comparisons and daily life
sourceSummary: Comparing things (plus/moins que, aussi... que) and reflexive verbs for a typical day.

questions.prompt: Choose the right comparison: "Mon frère est ___ grand ___ moi." (My brother is taller than me.)
questions.opener: "More ... than" is formed with plus ... que.
choices: plus ... que
aussi ... que
moins ... comme
plus ... comme
questions.explanation: "Plus ... que" means "more/-er ... than": "plus grand que moi" = "taller than me". "Aussi ... que" is used instead for "as ... as".

questions.prompt: What does "Ce livre est aussi intéressant que l'autre" mean?
choices: This book is more interesting than the other one
This book is less interesting than the other one
This book is just as interesting as the other one
This book is the most interesting
questions.explanation: "Aussi ... que" means "as ... as": the books are equally interesting.

questions.prompt: Which word is irregular in the comparative ("better")?
questions.opener: Just like Swedish "bra – bättre" (good – better) is irregular.
choices: plus bon
meilleur
plus meilleur
bonnement
questions.explanation: "Bon" (good) has the irregular comparative form "meilleur" (better), not "plus bon".

questions.prompt: What does "Je me lève à sept heures" mean?
questions.opener: Reflexive verbs are often used for daily routines.
choices: I go to bed at seven o'clock
I get up at seven o'clock
I eat breakfast at seven o'clock
I get home at seven o'clock
questions.explanation: "Se lever" means "to get up/rise", and "je me lève" is the present-tense form for "I": "I get up at seven o'clock".

questions.prompt: What does "Je me couche à dix heures et demie" mean?
questions.opener: Another common reflexive verb for daily routines.
choices: I shower at half past ten
I go to bed at half past ten
I eat dinner at half past ten
I leave home at half past ten
questions.explanation: "Se coucher" means "to go to bed", and "je me couche" is "I go to bed": "I go to bed at half past ten".

questions.prompt: Write the French verb for "to shower" in its base form (infinitive).
Correct the error: "Ma maison est plus petite que la tienne, mais mon jardin est plus bon."
questions.opener: "Bon" has its own irregular comparative form.
questions.answer: Ma maison est plus petite que la tienne, mais mon jardin est meilleur.
steps: "Plus bon" is wrong — "bon" is irregular in the comparative.
The correct form is "meilleur" (better), without "plus" in front of it.
Full sentence: "Ma maison est plus petite que la tienne, mais mon jardin est meilleur." (My house is smaller than yours, but my garden is better.)

questions.prompt: How do you form comparisons and describe a daily routine in French?
questions.opener: Comparison words and reflexive verbs for everyday life.
questions.answer: Comparisons: plus ... que = more ... than · moins ... que = less ... than · aussi ... que = as ... as · meilleur/pire = better/worse (irregular). Daily routine (reflexive verbs): se réveiller = wake up · se lever = get up · se doucher = shower · s'habiller = get dressed · prendre le petit-déjeuner = eat breakfast · se coucher = go to bed. Reflexive pronouns: me, te, se, nous, vous, se — placed before the verb: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève.
